card.title: What a QR code menu actually costs (including the parts nobody quotes)
card.excerpt: Pricing pages show one number. Your real cost includes setup time, per-location fees, order commissions and printing. Here's the full arithmetic.

h1: How much does a QR code menu cost?
intro: The advertised number is rarely the number you pay. Digital menu pricing splits into four models, and which one you're on matters more than the headline price — a €0 tool that charges commission on orders can cost more per month than a €20 subscription. Here's how to work out your real figure.

rows: Codes can expire; PDF is unreadable on a phone
Vendor branding or ads shown to your guests
Check whether it's per venue or per user
Cost rises exactly as your business grows

blocks.text: IQ Rest sits in the third row: **from €9.90 a month per venue**, no commission on orders, 14 days free without a card. We charge for the venue, not per waiter, because charging per user penalises exactly the venues with the most staff turnover.
The cost everyone forgets: getting the menu in

Typing 80 items with prices, descriptions and categories takes two to four hours. At a manager's fully loaded hourly cost, that's a real €40–€100 you spend before the menu exists — and you spend it again next season if the tool makes bulk edits painful.

This is why menu import matters more than it sounds. IQ Rest reads a photo of your paper menu and builds the items automatically, which turns that half-day into roughly five minutes. Budget the setup time when you compare tools; it's often larger than the first year of subscription.

items: **Table tents or stickers:** €1–€3 per table, one-off. A 20-table room is under €60.
**Reprinting:** €0 if the code points at a fixed address you control. This is the whole argument for a hosted menu.
**Guest devices:** €0. Guests use their own phones and install nothing.
**Kitchen screen:** €0 if you use a tablet you already have. A [kitchen display](route:/kitchen-display) runs in a browser, so a five-year-old tablet is enough.
**Wi-Fi:** worth checking. If guests can't get signal at the far tables, the menu doesn't load, and that's a plumbing problem no software fixes.

blocks.text: For comparison, one print run of laminated paper menus for the same room typically lands between €150 and €400, and most venues do three to six a year. The digital menu is usually cheaper in year one, before you count anything it does that paper can't.

items: **Per-location pricing across a group.** Five venues at €30 each is €1,800 a year. Ask about multi-venue rates before you sign for one.
**Order commission.** A 3% fee on €12,000 of monthly QR orders is €360 a month — thirty times a flat subscription.
**Payment processing.** Separate from the menu vendor and unavoidable if you take card payments at the table. Compare it against what your terminal already charges.

**Digital menu boards.** The screens behind the counter are a different product entirely — hardware, mounting and signage software push that into the thousands. A QR menu on the guest's own phone avoids all of it.

blocks.text: Before comparing prices, write down your monthly QR order volume. If it's near zero, commission models are cheapest. Past roughly €300–€500 of monthly orders, a flat subscription almost always wins.

Sometimes. A seasonal kiosk with eight items and fixed prices genuinely doesn't need a subscription. But read what "free" means in each case — ads shown to your guests, a code that dies when the trial ends, or a menu you can't export are all real costs that simply aren't on the invoice. We went through them one by one in [what a free QR menu really costs](blog:free-qr-code-menu).

items.q: How much does a QR code menu cost per month?
items.a: Flat-subscription tools generally run €10–€40 per venue per month. IQ Rest starts at €9.90 with no commission on orders.

items.q: Is there a free QR code menu?
items.a: Yes, several — usually funded by vendor branding shown to guests or by limiting you to a PDF. They work for a small, static menu and become expensive in other ways once you need updates, languages or ordering.

items.q: Do I pay per table or per restaurant?
items.a: With IQ Rest, per restaurant — tables and QR codes are unlimited. Check this before signing anywhere, because per-table and per-user pricing scales badly.
No. The menu import is included, and there is nothing to install for you or your guests.

items.q: What does a digital menu board cost instead?
items.a: That's a different category — screens, mounts and signage software, typically hundreds to thousands per screen plus installation. A QR menu uses the guest's phone and costs nothing in hardware.
